content.comment_body: Hello, I'm dealing with a similar issue, but mine is a bit more complex. I have a [product_name] [version_no], but the display is damaged and only shows some pixels, even though everything else works normally. I'm trying to use the scroll buttons to configure certain functions in the program, which I've already set up in the software using the C1 to C4 arrows. However, nothing happens, and I can't figure out why—mainly because I can't use the display. I have several questions: 1: I attempted a firmware update hoping it might restore the screen, thinking that if some pixels respond, it could be a firmware issue rather than hardware. However, the firmware did not change, as I confirmed through [product_name] [product_name]. Does updating the firmware ever fix a display problem? 2: How can I use the arrow keys as inputs when the display doesn't work? I need clear instructions for the button sequences required to perform operations without visual feedback. 3: I realize it's a big ask, but could someone share all the [product_name] [version_no] screen flows, perhaps as a flowchart, so I can understand what I'm doing on the device? Thanks a lot. -- Split from a previous discussion about using cursor keys.

To use the cursor keys to trigger a function (such as switching an output) inside a [product_name] program, hold down the ESC key and then press the corresponding cursor key. Note that you must have programmed at least one message text for this to work. Edit: A message text must also be actively displayed.

Instead of guessing, consider checking the operating instructions for your [product_name] controller. The documentation provides all menu flows as diagrams or flowcharts. If you need to access the system menu, that's challenging with a broken display. But, if you want to modify values in active messages, try enabling the webserver in message settings and their properties. That way, you can access virtual displays via a browser using BM and TDE models. Best regards, [user_name]

analysis.insight_summary: The central difficulty is operating a [product_name] [version_no] with a broken display, prompting the user to look for alternative means of managing settings and using physical buttons as inputs without seeing the menus. Uncertainty exists about whether firmware updates address hardware faults like display issues. Responses clarify necessary programming for button functionality and recommend consulting technical documentation or web-based tools for remote visualization.
analysis.user_expectations: The user hopes to reassign hardware button functions independently of the device's display and hopes firmware updates could restore lost functionality. They request comprehensive documentation or menu diagrams to assist with blind navigation and confirmation of input actions.
